checks: Vietnamese prose supports canonical inline math with accessible MathML
Legacy single-dollar formulas and double-dollar display math render once
Nested fractions, powers, subscripts and indexed roots use real mathematical markup
Aligned multi-step equations and systems render as separate display blocks
Sums, products, Greek, geometry and Vietnamese text remain supported
Display formulas embedded in a paragraph never create div-inside-p nesting
Markdown produces real headings, emphasis, ordered and unordered lists
Markdown tables keep pipe characters inside math/code and proper header semantics
Currency and escaped dollar pairs remain literal without accidental math
Explicitly paired numeric/decimal math renders while unpaired prices stay literal
Inline and fenced code protect dollars/backslashes/Markdown from rendering
Explicit math/latex code fences are formulas while ordinary code stays code
Bare common legacy commands and unmatched dollar-symbol command do not leak raw syntax
Legacy double-escaped paired math renders without globally decoding paths or code
Malformed bare math preserves the following explanation instead of swallowing it
Malformed/unsupported expressions show readable fallback instead of red/raw commands
Untrusted HTML is escaped text, never interpreted as HTML or script
Imported literal entities are not blindly decoded or interpreted as HTML
Markdown links are bounded to HTTP(S), blocked URLs never become clickable
Malicious KaTeX URLs/HTML/styles and macro state are rejected before rendering
Inline rendering remains phrasing-only inside an actual heading/button
Inline button content cannot introduce links or a nested formula tab stop
Very long math is bounded and oversized source gets an explicit display note
Many tiny formulas share one per-render budget across paragraphs and tables
Render and JSON reload are deterministic and preserve original source/citation offsets
Full lesson mixing Markdown/math/table/code is stable without a second rendering pass
Renderer imports and SSR never dispatch a network/provider call
